what: New validation-suite requirement from 2026-04-27: every supported editor needs an explicit Node-version-mismatch scenario in the E2E matrix, not just happy-path. Reason: memory #348's binding-mismatch silent-fail is tool-AGNOSTIC — any host that runs our hooks under a Node whose ABI differs from the postinstall-time Node hits the same silent failure. Cursor surfaced it first because their hook runtime (Node 22) differed from the user's nvm default (Node 18). Claude Code, Codex, Continue, etc. would all be vulnerable to the identical issue under any of: (a) nvm default switch after install, (b) Node major upgrade, (c) editor bundles its own Node that differs from terminal Node, (d) global vs local install with different ambient Node. **Required adds to E2E_VALIDATION.md:** (1) per-editor row "Node ABI mismatch surfaces clear error / self-heals (does NOT silently swallow)" — currently fails everywhere because dispatcher's catch absorbs the throw; (2) cross-editor row "User upgrades Node post-install → hooks still work without manual intervention" — depends on whatever auto-handling we ship per memory #pending. The validation suite must distinguish editor-specific platform issues from environment/packaging issues that affect every editor equally — without this distinction we'll keep mis-attributing bugs to "Cursor doesn't honor X" when the real cause is upstream of the editor.
why: User directive 2026-04-27: "we should also have a vlaidation scneario for node mismatch on cursdor , claude etc ... need to figure out if this is a tool agnositc issue or not." Without a Node-mismatch scenario in the matrix, we'll re-discover this class of bug per editor instead of treating it as an environment concern. Scoping to docs/validation/** so future E2E updates surface this requirement.
